podcast.body: Featured as the first cut on the "Saturday Night Fever" soundtrack, this disco hit was a highlight of the Bee Gees' 1979 concert special. When the band broke into this song during their Oakland concert, the crowd's reaction was described as overwhelming excitement. "Of course, that's the first cut on the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack."

podcast.body: Written by the Bee Gees in just two hours, "Stayin' Alive" became the theme song for "Saturday Night Fever." The band wrote it without knowing much about the movie, based on a request from Robert Stigwood for "eight minutes, three moods" – frenzy, passion, then wild frenzy. It was featured in the movie's trailer released in September 1977, generating high demand on radio before the soundtrack's official release. Frank Rose of Rolling Stone described it as "A Disco Tune, it has a real-gy precision like a sleek black Mercedes with an ash tray full of coke." "They wrote the song Stayin' Alive in two hours."
This song was one of four number one hits from the "Saturday Night Fever" soundtrack. "Stan Alive."

Written and performed by the Bee Gees, this song served as the iconic opening track for the film *Saturday Night Fever*. It became a number one hit in February 1978, holding the top spot for approximately a month, and earned a Grammy Award in 1979. Rolling Stone magazine included it at number 99 on its most recent list of the 500 Songs of All Time. "Staying alive, written by the Bee Gees, performed by the Bee Gees. It went to number one in February 1978."
